Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:

text:
This looks like late 2021: CPI at 6.88% YoY matches November 2021 (6.8%), and core CPI at 4.96% fits too. Unemployment at 4.2% matches November 2021, and the 10-year yield at 1.52% fits. US large-cap equity gained 5.8% in the month, consistent with November's rebound after a weak start, and the VIX at 17.33 is in line.

Two details point to a different month, but I read them as noise:
- Payrolls averaged 378k over 3 months, which is plausible for Sep–Nov 2021 after revisions.
- The 3-month change in the 2-year yield of +0.45 fits Nov 2021, when the 2-year was about 0.73%.

Equities rose in November 2021 by about 0.3%, not 5.8%, so the 1m equity return fits December 2021 better. December 2021 CPI was 7.0% and the unemployment rate was 3.9%, which does not match. The 2-year yield was 0.73% at end-November and the 10-year was 1.44%, close to the snapshot's 1.52%. The CPI and unemployment data therefore point to November, though the data may be as of a mid-month release. The 5.8% 1m equity return could come from a month-end date such as Dec 2021 (S&P up 4.5%). The 10-year at end-December was 1.52%, which matches exactly. The 2-year at end-December was 0.73%, which also matches. So the market data are December 2021, and the macro data show CPI of 6.88%, which is the November figure, still the latest published at the end of December. The unemployment rate of 4.2% is also the November figure.

My answer is December 2021.
